content:
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten on Monday revealed that Americans aren’t so hot on Donald Trump right now, with Google searches for the president hitting a second-term low and falling 48% from a year ago.

“I think the number one thing that the president of the United States fears than anything else — more than he fears than anything else — is becoming irrelevant,” Enten said.

He later continued, “He’s spending more time in the water than Katie Ledecky at this point.”

Aside from interest in Trump plummeting just weeks after the GOP’s midterm wipeout, new polling shows Republicans “absolutely” think he’s “on the verge of becoming a lame duck” president, Enten noted.

A majority of Republicans and Republican-leaning independents (72%) say Trump won’t be able to pass his policies over the next two years, per a recent survey by the Pew Research Center.

That’s a notable turn from the 2018 election — which brought a blue wave, too — when 55% of Republicans and Republican-leaning independents said the president would be able to pass his policies.

Later in the segment, Enten compared Trump’s sub-40% approval rating to those of Harry Truman and George W. Bush, who held similar figures at this point in their second term only for their approval ratings to never recover.

“We’ll have to wait and see what happens with Donald Trump, but history doesn’t look too kindly upon presidents who are already well underwater at this point,” he concluded.
